topic: Pointwise CATE minimax rate when the covariate density is merely bounded and unknown: prove that over the class with density unknown, unsmooth and confined to a fixed two-sided band, the minimax mean-absolute error at x_0 is strictly slower than the Kennedy-Balakrishnan-Robins-Wasserman rate r_n on a nonempty open low-smoothness region, hence strictly slower than the known-density minimax value, establishing the design density as a first-order component of the CATE minimax problem rather than a third-order nuisance absorbed by higher-order influence functions.

open_problems.open_problem: Over Hölder CATE classes with an unknown covariate density constrained only by fixed positive lower and upper bounds, is the pointwise minimax mean-absolute-error rate strictly slower than the Kennedy-Balakrishnan-Robins-Wasserman rate on a nonempty open low-smoothness region?

source_refs.claim: Their lower bound allows a merely bounded covariate density, but rate attainability needs additional density-estimation conditions; they explicitly call for future work on the density's role.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: For global missing-data and treatment-effect functionals, empirical HOIFs retain the original asymptotic guarantees without any smoothness condition on the covariate density.
source_refs.author: Lin Liu, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Whitney K. Newey, and James M. Robins

source_refs.excerpt: the Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman match uses a density/Gram-stable submodel
The KBRW nonprivate expression is not asserted as the established frontier of the full positive-density class
Impose 0<beta<=gamma and state the exact density-qualified Kennedy et al. comparison regime

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kennedy et al. deliberately prove their lower bound on a broad bounded-density model but attain the displayed rate only under stronger density-estimation and local Gram conditions, and the banked private-CATE run therefore refuses to treat that rate as the established frontier of the full positive-density class. The concrete obstacle is to couple oscillatory density perturbations with propensity and outcome-regression perturbations while preserving density normalization, overlap, Hölder restrictions, and mixture indistinguishability. Empirical HOIFs show that density smoothness can disappear for global average functionals, so it remains unresolved whether localization to roughly n h^d observations creates a genuine information loss or merely exposes a weakness of the published estimator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided minimax theorem over the band-only unknown-density class, with an explicit open set of (alpha,beta,gamma,d) on which its rate is polynomially slower than the known-density KBRW value, or a matching density-free upper bound proving that no such separation exists.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact Hölder pointwise-CATE model, regression/functional-hybrid narrative, rate phase diagram, and explicit unresolved density qualification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE is a regression/functional hybrid -> localized HOIFs attain the derived rate when the design law is estimable enough -> the lower-bound model permits only a bounded design density -> determine whether unknown unsmooth design changes the first-order minimax rate

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the localized fuzzy-hypotheses construction while perturbing the design density jointly with the causal nuisances, and compare it with the localized higher-order R-learner risk decomposition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the exact pointwise-CATE experiment whose lower and upper density scopes must be reconciled.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace density-based population projections by inverse empirical Gram matrices and prove bias and variance control without density smoothness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the strongest adjacent construction suggesting that density smoothness can be eliminated, and therefore the natural upper-bound competitor to a strict-slowdown converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the random-design U-statistic local-polynomial estimator and its sparse-allocation lower-bound construction, neither of which requires a smooth design density.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves a random-design minimax frontier for another regression/functional hybrid and explicitly constructs the design randomness needed in both halves of a matched theorem.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the pointwise CATE rate under a merely banded unknown design density be derived from one primitive Hölder law class, rather than assuming localization bias, effective local mass, nuisance rates, and perturbability as separate high-level inputs?

source_refs.excerpt: Restate the target as the smoothed functional theta_h(P), or add an explicit version/regularity condition
Three-channel localized Le Cam converse construction

open_problems.why_unsolved: The downgraded structure-agnostic CATE proposal encoded a three-channel rate only after taking the local bias, local effective mass, nuisance-learning rates, and a local-richness condition as primitives; its reviewer also caught that an unrestricted conditional mean at x_0 is not a law functional. A valid primitive theorem must impose enough CATE regularity to select a pointwise version while deriving local mass and Gram behavior uniformly from a design density with no modulus of continuity. The two-sided density band controls ball probabilities but does not directly supply the density-ratio approximation used by the published higher-order projection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A primitive-class minimax theorem that derives every localization, effective-sample, nuisance-interaction, and design-Gram term from explicit Hölder CATE/nuisance assumptions plus the two-sided density band, with feasible fuzzy or Le Cam alternatives for every leading branch.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides a well-defined Hölder pointwise target and the nearest primitive causal minimax formulation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE at a point requires local regularity -> localization trades approximation against effective sample size -> nuisance interaction creates a low-smoothness branch -> derive all channels uniformly when the local design law is unknown

method_exemplars.technique: Use the cross-fitted doubly robust pseudo-outcome and local-regression oracle inequality, then derive its normalization and product remainder from the primitive density class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the estimator skeleton whose high-level local inputs must be discharged.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the localized fuzzy-hypothesis construction and higher-order local-polynomial estimator, but prove class membership and Gram control uniformly over the larger design class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution asks for the same statement-level object with all design assumptions made primitive and scope-matched.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a density-free empirical or stabilized higher-order local R-learner attain the known-density pointwise CATE rate, and what projection-dimension threshold relative to the local sample size n h^d separates attainability from failure?

source_refs.claim: Their higher-order local R-learner attains the minimax lower-bound rate only under a condition ensuring sufficiently accurate estimation of the localized covariate law.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Empirical HOIFs bypass density estimation by learning an inverse sample Gram matrix, but their projection dimension must remain small relative to sample size.
source_refs.author: Lin Liu, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Whitney K. Newey, and James M. Robins

source_refs.claim: Stabilized HOIFs avoid sample splitting and control Gram instability for bilinear functionals, but do not analyze doubly localized pointwise CATE estimation.
source_refs.author: Na Liu, Chang Li, Yujia Gu, and Lin Liu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Density-based HOIFs allow a large population projection but require estimating an unsmooth law; empirical and stabilized HOIFs avoid density estimation but pay dimension-to-sample-size and random-matrix stability conditions. At x_0, localization replaces n by roughly n h^d and makes the basis itself bandwidth dependent. Existing global bilinear-form theory therefore does not determine whether the projection dimension required by the low-smoothness CATE branch fits inside the local sample or creates a new leading Gram-noise term.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A risk theorem for a density-free localized HOIF estimator with a sharp necessary-and-sufficient scaling condition on k/(n h^d), or a counterexample proving that every empirical-Gram construction fails to attain the KBRW rate in a stated low-smoothness regime.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation is organized around the exact density-estimation versus empirical-Gram instability tradeoff inherited by localized CATE estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Classical HOIFs require multivariate density estimation -> empirical HOIFs avoid density estimation but invert a large random Gram matrix -> stabilization controls that inversion for global bilinear forms -> determine whether stabilization survives CATE localization with effective sample n h^d

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the stabilized inverse-Gram construction, Neumann-series bias expansion, cancellation identities, and graph-counting variance bounds to a bandwidth-dependent local basis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof isolates precisely the Gram-estimation error that must be controlled after localization.

method_exemplars.technique: Use an independent empirical projection measure and inverse sample Gram matrix, then recompute the bias-variance frontier with n replaced by n h^d.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the foundational density-free empirical-HOIF construction and exposes the dimension restriction at issue.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain the local R-learning moment, bandwidth, and stretched projection basis while replacing the estimated population projection by a stabilized empirical one.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It fixes the exact causal target and risk decomposition into which the density-free Gram machinery must be inserted.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax expected length of an honest pointwise confidence interval for the CATE at x_0 over the two-sided-banded unknown-density class, and can that length be attained uniformly in the low-smoothness regime?

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes mean-absolute point-estimation risk but does not provide a pointwise limit law, honest confidence interval, or minimax expected-length theorem for its localized HOIF estimator.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: For scalar nonparametric-regression targets, bias-aware local-polynomial intervals have honest coverage and near-minimax efficiency under smoothness restrictions.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesár

source_refs.claim: Changing-kernel quadratic U-statistics can be asymptotically normal at slower-than-root-n rates, including high-dimensional nonparametric examples.
source_refs.author: James Robins, Lingling Li, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen, and Aad van der Vaart

open_problems.why_unsolved: The CATE-optimal statistic combines local-polynomial approximation bias, nuisance-product bias, and a bandwidth- and dimension-dependent degenerate U-statistic. Bias-aware regression intervals do not cover the higher-order causal remainder, while existing changing-kernel U-statistic CLTs do not include the random localized projection operator induced by an unknown unsmooth density. Uniformly calibrating bias, variance, and Gram failure over the density band is thus absent from both theories.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence-interval theorem with uniform 1-alpha coverage over the band-only class, a valid limit law or finite-sample calibration for the localized HOIF statistic, and a matching lower bound for worst-case expected interval length.

writing_exemplar.why: Its pointwise CATE phase diagram and estimator decomposition provide the natural setup before pivoting from optimal estimation to honest inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pointwise CATE estimation has a nonstandard minimax rate -> localized HOIFs can attain it under extra design control -> scientific use requires uncertainty quantification -> find honest intervals and their minimax length under unknown unsmooth design

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the conditional CLT for changing-kernel quadratic U-statistics dominated by a degenerate second-order component, with localized variance consistency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The higher-order local R-learner's stochastic leading term is a changing localized degenerate U-statistic rather than an ordinary regression average.

method_exemplars.technique: Port bias-aware critical values, modulus-based efficiency bounds, and MSE-optimal bandwidth calibration to the causal local moment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the honest-interval problem for the oracle pointwise-regression component under explicit smoothness restrictions.

open_problems.open_problem: Does one data-driven pointwise CATE estimator attain, up to the sharp unavoidable adaptation cost, the minimax rates across a nested scale from merely banded to Hölder-smooth unknown design densities?

source_refs.claim: Its attainable rate depends on the accuracy of covariate-law estimation, but tuning and density-estimation conditions are fixed rather than selected adaptively across design classes.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: A local-polynomial M-estimator with Lepski selection adapts to weakly specified unknown design and noise distributions and to the target's pointwise smoothness.
source_refs.author: Michaël Chichignoud and Johannes Lederer

source_refs.claim: Pointwise local-polynomial regression can adapt simultaneously to unknown local design mass and target smoothness, with minimax behavior governed by local design regular variation.
source_refs.author: Stéphane Gaïffas

open_problems.why_unsolved: The CATE risk depends jointly on CATE smoothness, two nuisance smoothness indices, localization bandwidth, projection dimension, and design-law or Gram approximation. Lepski selectors handle ordinary pointwise regression, but here the bias contains products of nuisance and density errors and the stochastic order changes across the regression/functional elbow. No cited theory compares this coupled family of localized HOIF candidates or establishes the unavoidable price of learning the density-regularity regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An oracle-inequality theorem for a data-driven bandwidth, projection-dimension, and Gram-stabilization selector that attains each design-class minimax rate up to an explicit factor, paired with a constrained-risk lower bound proving that factor sharp or simultaneous adaptation impossible.

writing_exemplar.why: Its elbow-shaped rate and density qualification naturally motivate an estimator that learns which side of the density-dependent frontier applies.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE minimax behavior changes across smoothness regimes -> attainability also depends on design-law accuracy -> density regularity is unknown in practice -> construct a rate-adaptive pointwise CATE procedure and identify its unavoidable cost

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over empirical-variance comparison and Lepski bandwidth selection, replacing ordinary local-polynomial candidates by localized HOIF estimators indexed by bandwidth, projection dimension, and stabilization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates pointwise minimax adaptation to weakly specified design and regression complexity in the oracle regression problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use local empirical-mass normalization and Lepski comparison to adapt to an unknown design law without first estimating a globally smooth density.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its random-design pointwise problem isolates the design-adaptation component that must be combined with causal orthogonalization.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its explicit bandwidth/projection risk decomposition as the candidate-wise deterministic bound in an oracle-selection proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact localized CATE estimator family and competing bias-variance branches the selector must compare.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2203.00837) derive the pointwise CATE minimax rate by localized fuzzy hypotheses and attain it with a localized HOIF R-learner only under extra covariate-law control.
Their lower-bound model allows the covariate density to be merely bounded, and the paper explicitly says future work should elucidate the density's role; this is the central lower/upper scope mismatch.
Kennedy (2023, Electronic Journal of Statistics, arXiv:2004.14497) gives oracle inequalities and local-polynomial R-learning rates but not the full minimax density frontier.
Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008, IMS Collections, arXiv:0805.3040) introduce HOIF U-statistics for optimal non-root-n point and interval estimation.
Robins, Li, Mukherjee, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2017, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1512.02174) formalize the HOIF projection bias-variance tradeoff in low-regularity models.
Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2017/2026 revision, arXiv:1705.07577) remove density smoothness for global average functionals using an empirical inverse Gram matrix.
Liu, Li, Gu, and Liu (2026, arXiv:2607.04743) stabilize empirical HOIF Gram inversion without sample splitting, but do not treat bandwidth-dependent pointwise CATE localization.
Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1902.10822) give a random-design U-statistic/local-polynomial minimax analysis requiring no design-density smoothness.
Gao and Han (2020, arXiv:2002.06471) derive random-design HTE rates with explicit covariate-geometry and density-ratio dependence, but in a two-sample matching model rather than the observational HOIF model.
Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2016, SPA, arXiv:1512.02280) prove slower-than-root-n CLTs for changing-kernel degenerate quadratic U-statistics.
Gaïffas (2007, ESAIM Probability and Statistics, DOI 10.1051/ps:2007023) adapts pointwise regression to unknown local design mass and target smoothness.
Chichignoud and Lederer (2014, Bernoulli, arXiv:1207.4447) construct pointwise local-polynomial estimators adaptive to weakly specified design/noise laws and regression smoothness.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2020, Quantitative Economics, arXiv:1606.01200) give honest, near-minimax-efficient bias-aware intervals for scalar pointwise nonparametric-regression targets.
The main tension is that density-free Gram methods succeed for global HOIF functionals while pointwise localization reduces the effective sample to n h^d and makes the basis bandwidth dependent.
No cited paper determines whether that localization yields a genuine CATE slowdown, an estimator-only obstruction, or a sharp design-regularity phase transition.
prior_proposal_map:
The highest-signal source was accepted stat_dp_cate_minimax_v1/holder_central_dp; its proto-core explicitly records that the KBRW expression is not established over the full positive-density class and that matching uses a density/Gram-stable submodel.
Its reviews/angle0_v2.json strengthening path requests the exact density-qualified KBRW comparison regime.
Downgraded stat_sa_cate_pointwise/v1 supplied reusable localized AIPW and three-channel Le Cam machinery, but its reviewer exposed point-target well-posedness and primitive-class deficiencies.
Accepted stat_dose_response_minimax/holder_anisotropic_converse was inspected and contains an analogous known-versus-unknown-density angle, but it was filtered out because its target is a continuous-dose partial mean rather than CATE.
Downgraded eid_dml_orthogonality_frontier/v1 and its rejected CATE/HOIF angles were inspected; their reviewer demanded primitive upper and lower arguments instead of assumed active channels.
No same-qid proposal, reviewer JSON, or rejected-angle archive existed yet under active/stat_cate_density_bottleneck.
The direct CATE bank evidence and the published KBRW future-work statement cross-link to the same unresolved nonprivate bounded-density frontier.
